quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Abyss Vent 101-1] Water near hydrothermal vents can reach temperatures of 350 degrees Celsius, which is high enough to melt lead. However, the extreme hydrostatic pressure at the bottom of the ocean prevents the water from boiling.
quests.question: The water near deep-sea hydrothermal vents remains liquid due to the extreme pressure, despite being hot enough to melt lead.
quests.hint: Check the last sentence discussing boiling and pressure conditions. (Diving calibration index 101-1)
quests.explanation: At great oceanic depths, immense pressure raises the water's boiling point, allowing it to reach superheated states while remaining liquid. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 101].

quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Coral Zone 101-2] Although coral reefs cover less than 0.1% of the world's ocean surface, they host and nurture over 25% of all marine life, earning them the nickname 'rainforests of the sea'.

quests.hint: Review the exact percentage of ocean surface area covered by reefs in the first sentence. (Diving calibration index 101-2)
quests.explanation: Coral reefs cover a tiny fraction (less than 0.1%) of the ocean surface, but concentrate an immense proportion of biodiversity. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 101].

quests.passage: [Biolum Lab 101-3] Bioluminescence is cold light produced chemically by deep-sea organisms. Unlike artificial lightbulbs, this biological light generates zero heat, allowing creatures to conserve vital energy.

quests.explanation: Bioluminescent light is known as 'cold light' because nearly 100% of the energy is emitted as light, generating no heat. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 101].

quests.passage: [Whale Pod 102-1] Blue whales are filter feeders that consume up to four tons of tiny krill every day. They do not possess teeth; instead, they have baleen plates that act as a giant sieve to trap food.

quests.passage: [Wave Pulse 102-2] In the open ocean, tsunami waves travel at speeds exceeding 800 kilometers per hour. As they approach shallow coastal waters, they slow down significantly but grow taller.

quests.explanation: Tsunamis slow down due to friction in shallow waters, causing the energy to compress and build tall, destructive wave heights. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 102].
